what_its_for: Monomethyl fumarate is used to treat relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS) in adults. This includes clinically isolated syndrome, relapsing-remitting MS, and active secondary progressive MS. It helps reduce the number of MS flare-ups (relapses) and slows the worsening of disability.
how_to_take: Swallow the capsules whole. Do NOT crush, chew, or open the capsules. You can take this medicine with or without food, but taking it with food may help reduce stomach upset. If stomach problems bother you, try taking it with a low-fat snack or meal. Take it at the same times each day to help you remember.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 95 mg taken by mouth twice daily (morning and evening) for the first 7 days. After that, the dose increases to 190 mg taken twice daily. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on how you respond and tolerate the medicine. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — as long as it is more than 4 hours before your next scheduled dose. If it is less than 4 hours until your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep the capsules in the original container and away from moisture and heat. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not store in the bathroom. Dispose of unused medicine properly — ask your pharmacist about take-back programs.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking other medicines that contain dimethyl fumarate (such as Tecfidera) at the same time, as this could increase your risk of serious side effects. Avoid drinking alcohol excessively, as it may worsen stomach side effects. Tell your doctor about all vitamins, supplements, and other medicines you are taking before starting this medication.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you notice: signs of a serious allergic reaction (rash, hives, trouble breathing, swelling of face or throat); signs of a rare but serious brain infection called PML (progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy) — new or worsening weakness on one side, clumsiness, vision changes, confusion, memory problems, or personality changes; signs of infection (fever, chills, body aches); unusual bruising or bleeding; severe or persistent nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea; signs of liver problems (yellowing of skin or eyes, dark urine, stomach pain); or flushing (redness, warmth, or tingling in the skin) that is very bothersome.
when_it_works: Monomethyl fumarate begins working in your body soon after you start taking it, but you may not feel or notice its effects right away. MS is a long-term condition, and this medicine works over time to help reduce relapses and protect your nervous system. It may take weeks to months before your doctor can measure its full benefit through tests and exams. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor, even if you feel well.
special_populations: Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. It is not fully known if this medicine is safe during pregnancy or passes into breast milk. Your doctor will help weigh the benefits and risks. Older Adults: Use with caution in elderly patients, as they may be more sensitive to side effects. Kidney or Liver Problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your dose or monitoring may need to be adjusted. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in children.
